original_card.first_experiment: Choose one assumption ID (native_all_columns, owned_erasure, compiler, precision_tape, analytic_recovery), one quantified implication and exact dependency closure. Check current handoffs, including #5625 row reentry and #5707 root-prefix lowering, without treating their partial scope as the whole theorem. Prove or falsify that implication with a caller-bound argument; stop at the chosen obligation. Finite tests or root digits do not discharge an all-size statement.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.

actual_scope: Sharp forward, inverse and arithmetic-noise norm envelopes for products whose interaction errors share an acyclic support graph of bounded path length.
scope_change_reason: The actual selected caller has no established common acyclic interaction-support contract. This is a new structured precision-interface theorem, rather than an audit or discharge of the selected precision_tape assumption.
bottleneck_link: A common acyclic interaction graph would replace conservative small-error or scalar-product precision budgets by exact finite polynomial envelopes. Binding that structure to a real caller and charging its arithmetic remain open.
stop_rule: Stop at the first proved sharp norm envelope and its exact attaining family; do not expand to caller construction or larger searches.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the all-finite-dimensional theorem. verify.py checks 326 polynomial coefficients, 729 exhaustive matrix pairs, 15 permuted words, 1553 prefixes and noisy steps, 51 attaining families, 20 input rejections and seven mathematical controls.

open_questions.question: Does one actual emitted local tile have a common acyclic interaction support in a usable fixed basis?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only that binding can make the sharp envelopes reduce an actual caller precision budget.
open_questions.first_step: Pin its exact prefixes F_i and actual coefficient-storage errors Delta_i; compute the union supports of F_i^-1 Delta_i F_(i-1), including the basis-change norm factors.
open_questions.blocked_by: A supplied coefficient-error and arithmetic-kernel contract, with paid basis changes and physical costs.

open_questions.question: What is the sharp budget for one particular acyclic graph when its forbidden paths rule out the shift-matrix witness?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The theorem is sharp over every graph of depth at most h, while an individual graph can admit a smaller precision envelope.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate its chronological supported paths and inverse within-factor path blocks for one fixed error-support schedule.
open_questions.blocked_by: Prescribed entry or norm budgets and an actual consumer decision; no additional graph census is supplied here.
